 Kumar Kushagra Family: Meet His Father Who Learnt Cricket From Books to Coach Him
 After his rescue act against Nepal in Doha, here’s a look at the family behind Jharkhand’s wicketkeeper-batter, from his self-taught coach father to his record-breaking rise. By Vanya Malhotra November 20, 2026 4 Mins Read

 Kumar Kushagra is one of the most promising wicketkeeper-batters in Indian cricket. The Jharkhand star is known for his calm head and solid technique, and he showed both again when he scored a match-turning century for India A against Nepal in the Asia Cup Rising Stars in Doha, coming in after early wickets and batting his side into a strong position.
 Innings like that have become a habit for Kushagra, but the story behind them goes back to his childhood in Bokaro. His father never played professional cricket, yet he taught himself the game from books so he could coach his son. Here is everything to know about Kumar Kushagra’s family, his parents, his coach and his journey in cricket.
 Kumar Kushagra Family Details
 Full name Kumar Kushagra 
 Date of birth October 23, 2004 
 Birthplace Ramnagar, Bokaro, Jharkhand 
 Father Shashikant 
 Mother Pushpa Devi 
 Siblings Younger brother Kalash and younger sister Sara 
 School Loyola School, Jamshedpur 
 College Kolhan University, Jamshedpur 
 First coach His father, Shashikant 
 Idol MS Dhoni 
 Domestic team Jharkhand 
 Role Wicketkeeper-batter 
 Kumar Kushagra’s Father Shashikant: The Man Who Coached Him
 Kushagra’s father, Shashikant, works as a District Commissioner in the GST department. He never played cricket at a professional level, but he is the biggest reason his son became a cricketer.
 When Kushagra was a young boy, cricket academies in Bokaro turned him away because he was too young. Instead of waiting, Shashikant decided to learn the game himself. He read cricket coaching books, including Bob Woolmer’s well-known The Art and Science of Cricket, and spent time watching players at the nets to understand their technique. He made a long list of shots and drills that he wanted his son to learn.
 He then set up practice nets at home and started coaching Kushagra himself. Because the academy nets were crowded in the evenings, father and son began training before sunrise. Shashikant would wake his son at 5 am, and they would practise for a couple of hours before school. Those early morning sessions, repeated for years, built the tight defence and patience that Kushagra is known for today.
 Kumar Kushagra’s Mother and Siblings
 Kushagra’s mother, Pushpa Devi, is a homemaker. While his father looked after the cricket side, she kept the home running and supported the early morning routine, which meant the whole family’s day started long before sunrise.
 Kushagra is the eldest of three children. He has a younger brother, Kalash, and a younger sister, Sara. The family has mostly stayed away from the spotlight, even as Kushagra’s name has grown in Indian cricket.
 Education and Early Cricket
 Kushagra was born in Ramnagar in Bokaro and later studied at Loyola School in Jamshedpur. He went on to pursue a BA from Kolhan University in Jamshedpur while playing cricket for Jharkhand.
 He started out purely as a batter. He took up wicketkeeping later, after watching and studying MS Dhoni closely. Coming from Jharkhand, comparisons with Dhoni were always going to follow him, and he has handled them well.
 Kushagra made an early impression in age-group cricket, playing for Bokaro at the Under-14 level and getting picked for Jharkhand’s Under-16 side at just 12. His run-scoring in junior cricket earned him a place in India’s squad for the 2020 Under-19 World Cup.
 The Record Innings That Changed Everything
 Kushagra’s big breakthrough came in the Ranji Trophy in 2022. Playing for Jharkhand against Nagaland, he turned his maiden first-class hundred into a huge double century. At just 17, he became the youngest batter to score 250 or more in a first-class innings, breaking a record held by Pakistan great Javed Miandad for decades.
 That innings made the whole country take notice. It led to a big IPL contract with Delhi Capitals, and he later moved to Gujarat Titans. Over the following seasons, he became one of Jharkhand’s most reliable batters across all formats and helped the side win the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy.
 A Calm Head in a Crisis
 Kushagra’s century scoring 117 off just 102 balls against Nepal in Doha summed up his game. With India A in early trouble, he did not panic. He took his time, built a big partnership with captain Tilak Varma, and then shifted gears once he was set. It was the same patience his father had worked on in those early morning sessions years ago.
 For the boy who was once turned away from a cricket academy for being too young, the journey from home nets in Bokaro to representing India A has been remarkable. And with a family that has backed him every step of the way, Kumar Kushagra looks ready for much bigger things.
